Vaccination remains the most effective prevention. To ease throat pain, rinse with warm saltwater (200 ml warm water with half a capful of salt), get ample sleep, sip warm fluids, keep indoor air humid, and avoid irritants or loud talking. Folk remedies like scallion water, pear soup, vitamin C, and foot baths may ease symptoms but do not halt illness progression. Seek medical care if throat pain worsens, swallowing or breathing becomes difficult, neck swelling, high fever, or marked weakness to rule out bacterial tonsillitis or influenza.

articleSummary: NOVOSIBIRSK, Nov 5 — Russian scientists at the Vector Virology Center have developed and patented the first test system in Russia for rapid detection of RNA from the highly pathogenic avian influenza A/H5N6 virus. The system targets both hemagglutinin (H5) and neuraminidase (N6) genes in a single real-time RT-PCR assay, requiring the simultaneous presence of both targets to confirm infection. If a related virus is present, the assay identifies it and indicates which component was detected. Results are generated in one tube with fluorescent probes that illuminate during amplification, enabling real-time monitoring and faster, simpler analysis. At the time, no Russian commercial kits for A/H5N6 existed; the new system reportedly covers all circulating H5N6 strains. Since 2013, A/H5N6 has caused over 1,000 poultry outbreaks, mainly in China and Southeast Asia; 93 human infections since 2014, 57 deaths (61%). The WHO flagged these viruses as a major pandemic threat in 2016.

articleSummary: Monkeypox is a DNA virus in the Orthopoxvirus group, related to smallpox. Endemic in central to western Africa, it has spread to other regions. Animal-to-human transmission occurs via direct contact with blood, secretions, or lesions, or through undercooked meat from infected animals such as primates and rodents. Human-to-human transmission occurs through direct contact with lesions or bodily fluids, respiratory droplets, kissing or sex, contaminated objects, or maternal-fetal transmission. Incubation is about 5–21 days. Prodrome (1–5 days) includes fever, chills, headache, myalgia, fatigue, and notable lymphadenopathy, distinguishing it from smallpox. The rash then appears on the face and spreads to the body, including palms and soles; lesions progress from red spots to vesicles, pustules, crusts, and crusting. Prevention: safe sex, masks, avoid wildlife contact, ensure meat is fully cooked, avoid sharing items, wash hands, and launder clothing and bedding. Thailand notes smallpox vaccination ended in 2019.

articleHeadline: A minimal 13-Transcript signature for HIV-TB coinfection in African children - Communications Medicine
articleSummary: A 13-transcript RNA-based signature discriminates HIV-TB coinfection from HIV mono-infection in African children. Whole-blood RNA-seq from Uganda (discovery, n=59) and Southern Africa (Botswana, Eswatini; cross-regional test cohort, n=38) identified DETs; an independent adult HIV-TB cohort from India (n=25) provided an external test. Using DESeq2 and recursive feature elimination, followed by Random Forest, the minimal 13-transcript panel achieved a cross-validated AUC of 0.865 in the Ugandan discovery set; in the Southern Africa cross-regional test cohort, AUC was 0.943 (95% CI 0.858-0.992) with all NoTB cases correctly classified (specificity 1.000, 95% CI 0.806-1.000). In Indian adults, performance was modest (AUC 0.773, 95% CI 0.564-0.929). Nine transcripts converge on neutrophil degranulation, and the signature outperforms neutrophil proportions alone. articleSummary: Salvador, Brazil recorded 8.6 hepatitis B cases per 100,000 in 2025, 65% above the national average of 5.2, with Bahia totaling 610 cases that year (Ministry of Health data). If infection clears within six months, it is cured and immune; otherwise it can become chronic, gradually injuring the liver over 20–30 years. Chronic infection risk is about 90% in newborns and under 5% in healthy adults. Vaccination is free through the SUS for all ages, and testing is recommended for unvaccinated adults at least once. Rapid finger-prick tests yield results in 30 minutes; positives require confirmatory testing. Confidentiality is protected by law 14.289/2022. Free care is available at the Faculdade de Medicina Zarns Salvador clinic.

articleSummary: In Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, a six-month cross-sectional study (July 3–December 5, 2025) evaluated rubella infection and maternal immunity among 124 pregnant women attending prenatal clinics (Bissita, Kombo Matari, Jeanne, Plateau Medical-Social Center). articleSummary: Cutaneous leishmaniasis, transmitted by the bite of an infected sandfly, presents as a non-healing skin lesion that may resemble a pimple and often causes little or no pain, delaying care. Lesions typically appear on exposed areas (arms, legs, face) with raised borders. Weeks to months may elapse between bite and lesion; travel history to farms, chacaras, or forested areas should be noted during consultation. In some cases, nasal or oral involvement can develop months to years later after skin healing, with symptoms such as nasal congestion, nosebleeds, or mouth ulcers. Transmission is not person-to-person. Seek evaluation at a Basic Health Unit (UBS) in Brazil; the public SUS offers free treatment. Prevention includes using repellents, covering arms and legs, screens, and removing organic debris around homes, especially at dusk and night when sandflies are active, per infectologist Alexandre Bertucci of Humap-UFMS in Campo Grande.

articleSummary: Persistent cough lasting more than two weeks in Jakarta, Indonesia, may signal tuberculosis (TB) and requires medical attention.
